lines.japanese: 僕の恋人を紹介しよう。
lines.english: Let me introduce my girlfriend.

lines.japanese: もう知ってるとは思うけれど、しばしば強さと儚さの両極に投げだされてしまう彼女の危うさは、どれだけ語ろうと語りつくせることはない。
lines.english: I am sure you already know her, but no amount of explanation could ever exhaust the precarious nature that so often hurls her between the extremes of strength and fragility.

lines.japanese: その危うさをも含めて、僕は彼女を愛している。
lines.english: I love that part of her too.

lines.japanese: 不謹慎を承知で、誤解を恐れず言えば、そのまますべて彼女のミステリアスな魅力とも捉えられるんだ。
lines.english: At the risk of sounding insensitive or being misunderstood, one could even see all of it as part of her mysterious charm.

lines.japanese: だから、焦らない。
lines.english: So I will not rush her.

lines.japanese: いましばらく時間はかかるかもしれないけれど、ふたりでゆっくり克服していこうと約束した。
lines.english: It may take a while longer, but we promised to overcome it slowly, together.

lines.japanese: それが僕の恋人、山科京ちゃん。
lines.english: That is my girlfriend, Miyako Yamashina.

lines.japanese: 巷の新年ムードもだいぶ薄れた一月のなかば。
lines.english: It was the middle of January, when the city’s New Year’s mood had largely faded.

lines.japanese: ともに難儀な事情を抱えた僕らが、愛の名のもとに、寄りそい支えあって生きてゆこうと誓ってから……ほぼ一ヵ月。
lines.english: Almost a month had passed since the two of us, each burdened by difficult circumstances, vowed in the name of love to live on by standing close and supporting each other.

lines.japanese: すでに僕らは、お互いの家族公認の付き合いになっていた。
lines.english: Our relationship already had the blessing of both our families.

lines.japanese: 京ちゃんの両親は共働きだから、病床の娘を終日看ているというのも難しい。
lines.english: Miyako’s parents both worked, so it was difficult for them to watch over their bedridden daughter all day.

lines.japanese: だから、しばしば病気の発作に見舞われたとき、彼女は羽田の家で療養するようになっていた。
lines.english: For that reason, whenever her illness struck, she had begun recuperating at the Haneda house.

lines.japanese: この種の疾患に理解と優しさのある僕の家族は、その都度とても温かく京ちゃんを迎えてくれる。
lines.english: My family understood this kind of condition and showed her great kindness. Each time, they welcomed Miyako with genuine warmth.

lines.japanese: 早く孫の顔が見たい、なんていう叔母さんの冗談には、くすぐったい恥ずかしさを覚えるけれど。
lines.english: Though my aunt’s jokes about wanting to see her grandchildren soon filled me with an oddly ticklish embarrassment.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 朝、居間へ下りるなり、小鳩が走りよってきた。
lines.english: The moment I came downstairs to the living room that morning, Kobato ran up to me.

lines.japanese: 無力感の波に呑まれた京ちゃんが羽田邸へ来て、三日。
lines.english: Three days had passed since Miyako, swallowed by a wave of helplessness, arrived at the Haneda residence.

lines.japanese: いま彼女はあらゆる意欲を奪われ、安らかな眠りさえ享受できぬまま、重苦しい絶望に押しつぶされている。
lines.english: Now every trace of motivation had been stripped from her, and a crushing despair bore down on her without even granting her the refuge of peaceful sleep.

lines.japanese: ほとんど眠れないのにベッドからも起きあがれない彼女の容体を、羽田家のみんなはとても心配してくれているんだ。
lines.english: She could barely sleep, yet could not rise from bed. Everyone in the Haneda family was deeply worried about her condition.

lines.japanese: 小鳩が何か聞いてくるより先に、僕はふたり分のありがとうを伝えた。
lines.english: Before Kobato could ask anything, I thanked her on behalf of both of us.

lines.japanese: そして、彼女が今朝もまだベッドに伏していることを。
lines.english: Then I told her that Miyako was still in bed that morning.

lines.japanese: 「え、大丈夫？」
lines.english: “Oh. Is she all right?”

lines.japanese: 「……じゃないんだよね」
lines.english: “...No, she isn’t.”

lines.japanese: 「うん……昨日も薬は飲んでたし、まだ残りもあると思うんだけど……さっき水も届けてきたし」
lines.english: “No... She took her medicine yesterday, and I think she still has some left... I brought her water a little while ago too.”

lines.japanese: 「今日は家に誰も居なくなっちゃうから、おれが側についててあげようと思って」
lines.english: “No one else will be home today, so I thought I’d stay by her side.”

lines.japanese: 僕は進学クラスに所属しているから、三月の卒業まではほぼ自由登校が認められていた（もっとも、僕は進学志望じゃないのだけれど）。
lines.english: I was in the college-track class, so until graduation in March I was permitted nearly complete freedom in whether to attend school—though I did not intend to go to college.

lines.japanese: 「優しいね」
lines.english: “You’re so kind.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、そんなことないよ。うん、まあ、普通かな」
lines.english: “Oh, no, not really. Yeah, well, pretty normal, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「私もなるべく早く帰ってくるから」
lines.english: “I’ll come home as early as I can too.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、平気だよ。おれが側についてるし、その……」
lines.english: “Ah, that’s all right. I’ll be here with her, and...”

lines.japanese: 「自分のために小鳩が早く帰ってきたなんて勘付かれたら、また深く沈んでいっちゃうから……」
lines.english: “If she realizes you rushed home early for her sake, she might sink even deeper...”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そうでした」
lines.english: “R-right. I forgot.”

lines.japanese: 小鳩は慌てて首を横に振った。そのあとすぐ、謝るために今度は縦に振る。
lines.english: Kobato hastily shook her head, then immediately nodded it to apologize.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい、まだ勉強不足で」
lines.english: “I’m sorry. I still don’t know enough.”

lines.japanese: 「全然。そんなこと言わないでよ」
lines.english: “Not at all. Don’t say that.”

lines.japanese: 謝られるどころか、僕は妹に感謝していた。彼女は、兄の恋人の病気に対して理解を示してくれている。
lines.english: Far from wanting an apology, I was grateful to my little sister. She made an effort to understand her brother’s girlfriend’s illness.

lines.japanese: 一緒に暮らしていて「面倒だ」とか「また？」なんて言葉を一度だって口にしたことがない。
lines.english: Even while sharing her home, Kobato had never once said anything like, “What a pain,” or, “Again?”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう小鳩」
lines.english: “Thank you, Kobato.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん。お大事にって伝えて……あ、あわっ、これも駄目なんだった」
lines.english: “Y-yeah. Tell her I hope she feels—oh! Th-that was wrong too.”

lines.japanese: 「あはっ」
lines.english: “Ahaha.”

lines.japanese: 「わ、笑ったらしつれい」
lines.english: “I-it’s rude to laugh.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ごめん、そうだよね。おれの恋人のことなのに」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. You’re right. This is my girlfriend we’re talking about.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そじゃなくて、慌てる私を笑うのがしつれい」
lines.english: “Th-that’s not what I meant. It’s rude to laugh at me for getting flustered.”

lines.japanese: 「あははっ」
lines.english: “Ahahaha.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、笑ったー！」
lines.english: “You laughed again!”

lines.japanese: そんな他愛ない会話をしながら、僕は小鳩を玄関まで見送った。
lines.english: We traded that harmless banter as I saw Kobato to the front door.

lines.japanese: 「いつもと逆だね。いってらっしゃい」
lines.english: “We’ve switched places today. Have a good day.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。いってきます」
lines.english: “Okay. See you later.”

lines.japanese: ドアが閉まると急に静かになった。話し相手がいなくなったんだから当然か。
lines.english: The house fell abruptly silent when the door closed. That was only natural, now that I had no one to talk to.

lines.japanese: それにしても静かすぎる。きっと京ちゃんは、今でも布団の中で丸くなっているんだろう。
lines.english: Still, it was too quiet. Miyako was surely curled beneath the covers even now.

lines.japanese: 僕が側にいてあげなくちゃ。
lines.english: I had to stay by her side.

lines.japanese: 彼女が沈んでしまっているときはどんな言葉も届かない。それでも、どんなに邪魔者扱いされても、側にいてあげることで、少しでも彼女の役に立ちたいんだ。
lines.english: When she sank this low, no words could reach her. Even so, no matter how much she treated me as a nuisance, I wanted to help her in whatever small way I could simply by remaining close.

lines.japanese: そんなことを考えて、二階を見上げたときだった。
lines.english: I was thinking this as I looked up toward the second floor.

lines.japanese: 静かどころか、僕の部屋の襖が勢いよく開く音がした。続いて駆け足。
lines.english: Far from silence, I heard the sliding door to my room fly open, followed by running footsteps.

lines.japanese: 危ない、階段を踏みはずしてすっ転んだら大怪我になる。僕は危険を感じて、彼女が下りてくるよりも早く、二階まで駆けあがった。
lines.english: That was dangerous. If she missed a step and tumbled down the stairs, she could be badly hurt. Sensing the danger, I raced upstairs before she could come down.
“Mi—”

lines.japanese: 「おっっっはよーマイダーリン！　私、起きたよいま起きたよ、昨日なかなか寝付けなくて最後に時計みたの４時だったけど、いま時計見たら朝だからすなわちフェスティボー！」
lines.english: “Goooood morning, my darling! I’m awake, I just woke up! I couldn’t get to sleep forever last night and the last time I looked at the clock it was four, but now I looked and it’s morning, which therefore means festival!”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: 予想していたのとはあまりに違う恋人の様子に、うっかり声をあげてしまった。
lines.english: My girlfriend’s state differed so completely from what I expected that a cry escaped me.

lines.japanese: 「うっそサプライズイズ私！？　それすなわちフェスティボー？」
lines.english: “No way, is the surprise me?! Does that therefore mean festival?”

lines.japanese: 「み、京ちゃん。大丈夫なの、起きてきて。ちゃんと寝てないと……」
lines.english: “M-Miyako. Are you sure you should be up? You need to get some proper sleep...”

lines.japanese: 「うっそやだ！　え、それ心配？　ダーリン私のこと心配？　鋼鉄の私の身体の心配なんてミジンコもいらないけど、ダーリンがしてくれるのって偉大なる私への崇拝？」
lines.english: “No way, oh my gosh! Wait, are you worried? Darling, are you worried about me? My steel body doesn’t need one single speck of worrying, but when my darling worries, is that worship of the mighty me?”

lines.japanese: 「だけど山科京は平気だよ。太陽が偉そうに幅きかせてるからね。あいつに負けて布団の中へ逃げこんだと思われるのも癪だからね。山科京は恒星なんかに負けないよ。♪オー・ソーレ・ミーオ、ラららァ～！」
lines.english: “But Miyako Yamashina is fine! The sun’s throwing its weight around like it owns the place. I’d hate to let it think it beat me and sent me running under the covers. Miyako Yamashina doesn’t lose to some star! ♪ O sole mio, la la laaa!”

lines.japanese: 「うん、元気そうだね。でもほら、昨日はダウンの波がすごかったからさ」
lines.english: “Yes, you seem energetic. But you were hit by such a bad low yesterday.”

lines.japanese: だけど今の彼女は、ダウンどころかその……随分と楽しそうだ。
lines.english: Yet now she was not down at all. If anything... she seemed enormously cheerful.

lines.japanese: ダウンの次にはアップの波がくる。しばらくはダウンの大きな波が続いてたから、その反動がきてるのかもしれない。
lines.english: After a low came a high. Her lows had been intense for a while, so perhaps this was the rebound.

lines.japanese: ダウンもそうだけど、アップの波に乗っている彼女も一人にはしておけないんだ。今だって僕が駆けつけなければ、階段を転がりおちてきたかもしれない。
lines.english: I could not leave her alone during a high any more than I could during a low. If I had not rushed over just now, she might already have tumbled down the stairs.

lines.japanese: 「もうちょっと寝てた方がいいんじゃないかな……」
lines.english: “Maybe you should sleep a little longer...”

lines.japanese: 僕は安静にしてくれることを願った。とは言ってはみたものの、それが無駄なんてこともよく分かってる。
lines.english: I hoped she would rest. Even as I suggested it, however, I knew perfectly well that the suggestion was futile.

lines.japanese: 「え、寝るの！　寝たらすごいよ私！　昨日の夜も必死に寝ようとしてたからね。昨日はお昼から寝ててちっとも眠くなんてなかったけど、うんまあ４時くらいまで起きて結局は寝たよね」
lines.english: “What, sleep?! You should see me when I sleep! I tried so desperately to sleep last night. I’d been sleeping since noon yesterday, so I wasn’t tired at all, but, yes, I stayed up until around four and finally did sleep.”

lines.japanese: 「でもでもいま目覚めてるでしょ？　頭クリア？　私、透きとおってる？　中枢神経つまんでピーン！みたいな？　私やっぱり有象無象とは違うよね。意識の高揚だけでパキれるよね。それ、わっしょいわっしょい！」
lines.english: “But I’m awake now, right? Is my head clear? Am I transparent? Like somebody pinched my central nervous system and pulled it taut? I really am different from the teeming masses. I can get wired on elevated consciousness alone. Heave-ho! Heave-ho!”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、わっしょーい」
lines.english: “Ahaha. Heave-ho!”

lines.japanese: アップの波がきた京ちゃんは、それはそれで放っておけないけど、食事をとってくれるという意味ではダウンのときより体には優しいと思ってる。
lines.english: I could not leave Miyako alone when a high hit either, but in one respect it was kinder to her body than a low: she would eat.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、まずは朝ごはん食べよっか。小鳩が学校に出ちゃったから、おれの作ったものになっちゃうけど」
lines.english: “Then let’s start with breakfast. Kobato already left for school, so you’ll have to settle for something I make.”

lines.japanese: 「うそ、ごはん！？　言ってよ、わたし作るよ、鷹志君のためだもん。冷蔵庫の中身を全て駆使して作るよ。ポッポちゃんには劣るかもしれないけど、そこらの料理人には遅れを取らない朝食を作るよ」
lines.english: “No way, breakfast?! You should’ve said something. I’ll make it. It’s for you, Takashi! I’ll use everything in the fridge. I may not measure up to Poppo, but I’ll make you a breakfast that could beat any ordinary chef!”

lines.japanese: 「相変わらず京ちゃんのリスペクト小鳩はすごいね。でも冷蔵庫の中身を全部使うと叔母さんや小鳩が困っちゃうから、やっぱりおれが作るよ」
lines.english: “Your respect for Kobato is as impressive as ever, Miyako. But if you use everything in the fridge, my aunt and Kobato will be in trouble, so I’ll make it after all.”

lines.japanese: 「やだすごい！　鷹志君が私のために愛情手料理？　わたし愛されてる？　やだもー、そこまで言われると胸が張りさけそうだよ。さっきから交感神経パキってて、物理的にも心臓の血管が張りさけそうだからね」
lines.english: “Oh my gosh! Takashi is cooking for me with love? Am I loved? Oh, stop, when you put it that strongly, my heart could burst. My sympathetic nerves have been crackling this whole time, so the blood vessels around my heart might literally burst too.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、京ちゃんが苦しい目にあうようなことは困るかな」
lines.english: “Hmm. I’d rather you didn’t suffer, Miyako.”

lines.japanese: 「やだわたし愛され上手ミヤコ！」
lines.english: “Oh my gosh, I’m Miyako, born to be loved!”

lines.japanese: 「鷹志君、優しい……そんなに優しくされたら、ときめくよ湧きあがるよ盛りあがるよ、ＤＯＫＩがムネムネ君に胸キュンして、ロマンティックがとまらないよ」
lines.english: “Takashi, you’re so sweet... If you’re that sweet to me, my heart’ll race, I’ll bubble up, I’ll boil over! My thumpy is going heart-heart for you, and there’s no stopping the romance!”

lines.japanese: 「ア、アガってきた……やばいよこれ止まらない、ああもう落ちつかないよどーしよー」
lines.english: “I-it’s building... This is bad, it won’t stop. Ahh, I can’t settle down! What do I do?”

lines.japanese: 京ちゃんは地団駄踏むように足をドタバタし始めた。そんな彼女の肩を抱きながら、一緒に階段を下りる。
lines.english: Miyako began stamping her feet as though throwing a tantrum. Holding her by the shoulders, I descended the stairs with her.

lines.japanese: 僕が台所へ入って、卵を割ったところで京ちゃんは歌いはじめた。いい具合に焼けてきたところで僕の周りを回りはじめた。
lines.english: I entered the kitchen and cracked an egg. Miyako started singing. When the egg had begun to cook nicely, she started circling around me.

lines.japanese: 「♪オー・ソーレ・ミ～オォ～！　♪オー・ソーレ・ミ～オォ～！」
lines.english: “♪ O sole miooo! ♪ O sole miooo!”

lines.japanese: 「はは、京ちゃんはお腹すいてる？」
lines.english: “Ahaha. Are you hungry, Miyako?”

lines.japanese: 「おなペコ！」
lines.english: “Starving-Marvin!”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっと待っててね、すぐ出来るから」
lines.english: “Wait just a moment. It’ll be ready soon.”
“Uuugh...”

lines.japanese: けれど失敗だった。京ちゃんに食欲があるのなら、僕も先に済ませないで一緒に食べればよかったんだ。
lines.english: But I had made a mistake. If Miyako had an appetite, I should not have eaten earlier. I should have waited and eaten with her.

lines.japanese: 「やだもう我慢できない！　この昂りを抑えることなんて出来ないよ！」
lines.english: “Oh my gosh, I can’t take it anymore! I can’t hold back this rush!”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……わあっ！」
lines.english: “Wha—whoa!”

lines.japanese: 京ちゃんは料理をしていた僕の腰にしがみついてきた。下半身の制御を失い、僕はその場へ尻餅をついた。
lines.english: As I cooked, Miyako clung to my waist. My legs gave out, and I landed on my backside.
